OPCODES.md must not record these as done.

Polygon's parallel state lead (L-1254, answers read from other transactions of the same block in the BlockSTM multi-version store) was not worked again (established-l1 profile for 137 L2). The publicnode endpoint answered three of the five private bor builds of cycle 37 (cb3d19c5f690, a863b8e5cce1, 280514fa9fb7), so results for the other two rest on cycle 37.

The official endpoints of Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM and Arc still serve no block simulation, and no unit looked for mined evidence instead. Whether the block producers themselves wipe transient storage between transactions rests on source reading (Monad, revm versions pinned by mega-evm and nanoreth) and on third-party endpoints or replicas.

The cycle 38 sweep of 337 special addresses ran only the empty, balanceOf and transfer shapes. The IHooks selector shapes with caller-chosen hookData (P5) were last run against these addresses in cycle 2, when only 0x10, 0x64, 0x70, 0x74, 0xc8, 0x100 and 0x800 had a valid flag combination (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127). The sweep is cheap to extend to P5 and should be run with the others.

The mined swap check is thin on both: Avalanche had 36 swaps in its window this cycle and HyperEVM had none (two Swap logs in 100,000 blocks). For these networks the results come from eth_call and replicas, not from the producer.

leads.question: OPCODES.md (line 782 and the HyperEVM item after it) sets aside the PoolManager sites that the closed or compiled producers have never run, because only a pool the attacker creates reaches them and a wide amount cannot be settled. For each such site (the fee mulDiv at src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:64-65, the wide branches of SqrtPriceMath.sol:208-209 and 250-252, Position.sol:94-96, donate and exact output), can an ordinary account reach it in a hookless pool it creates from two currencies that other pools already hold, with an amount it can pay, and which wrong word at that site would raise amountOut, feeGrowthGlobal (src/libraries/Pool.sol:404-405 and 446) or a position's owed fees above what was paid? Write the answer per site as the word that would have to be wrong and the line where it reaches the shared balance.
leads.why: Both halves of the dismissal are untested. All pools of a currency draw on one balance (A6), so a fault in a pool the attacker created pays out other LPs' funds through take or collect (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). The cycle 38 answer to L-1333 already showed the fee site reached on HyperEVM in existing pools with a settleable amount. If any site passes this test, the producers that never ran it are within an ordinary account's reach.

leads.question: Apply the L-1333 method of cycle 38 to MegaETH: send the 24 wide exact input swaps (amountSpecified from -2^236 to -(2^255-1)) by eth_call through the deployed PoolManager 0xacb7e78fa05d562e0a5d3089ec896d57d057d38e against three existing hookless pools, on mainnet.megaeth.com and on a stateless validator node, and search the validated blocks from 7,009,653 to head for any PoolManager swap whose exact input magnitude has a fee product of 2^256 or more. Do the words match the reference, and has the producer ever executed that branch?
leads.why: The MegaETH line of OPCODES.md rests on 'a wide amount cannot be settled', which L-1333 contradicts for the fee site. The producer is a closed JIT (F-118), so mined evidence is the only test of the code that writes state.

leads.question: On the official producers, find mined evidence that transient storage is wiped between transactions: a block where one transaction calls PoolManager.sync(X) for an ERC-20 X and ends without a settle, followed in the same block by a PoolManager transaction that settles native value without its own sync and succeeds. Use replica traces on HyperEVM, the stateless validator on MegaETH, debug_traceBlockByNumber where any Monad or Arc endpoint allows it, or calldata decoding of Multicall and router transactions otherwise. Does such a pair exist on each network?
leads.why: These endpoints refuse eth_simulateV1, so the 23 multi-transaction scenarios never ran against the code that produces blocks. A successful native settle after a bare sync in the same block shows the producer cleared the synced currency (F-071 path, src/PoolManager.sol:349-356).

leads.question: What changed in hl-node around the 16 November 2026 announcement that asked nanoreth operators to update for compatibility, which nanoreth commit or release answers it, and does that change touch block execution (precompile set, system transaction handling, the EVM version, gas rules) or only the block format? The hyperevm unit found the nanoreth master Cargo.lock unchanged since cycle 36 and did not read the change itself.
leads.why: Replica re-execution is the only evidence of what the closed producer computes. If the producer changed and the replicas changed with it, earlier replica comparisons may describe an older producer.

leads.question: Read EIP-8037 at its current text and the Glamsterdam meta EIP. Does the state gas reservoir change the value the GAS opcode returns, or the 63/64 amount a CALL forwards, so that call(gas(), ...) at src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134 forwards less than today? Which of the 21 networks have a dated plan to adopt it (Ethereum Hoodi on 15 December 2026, any ArbOS proposal, Tempo T15, OP Stack and reth based chains), and does any caller-chosen gas split let a victim's hook call or payout fail while the outer call succeeds?
leads.why: Merges the arbitrum-family and Tempo EIP-8037 leads. Every failed sub-call in src/ reverts the whole call today, so the expected result is a freeze of the caller's own transaction only; the reading is needed before the first network adopts the rule.

leads.question: Transfer of F-165 (erigon's per-frame storage read cache) to the other go-ethereum family clients: do bor develop and the bor v2.11.1 tag, bsc v1.8.2 and libevm a335c2ecf4df carry any cache of SLOAD or TLOAD results in front of the StateDB, per frame, per interpreter or per BlockSTM worker, and if so what invalidates it on a nested write and on a revert?
leads.why: erigon shipped such a cache in v3.8.0 to v3.8.2 without a public note. Polygon already has two shared caches in front of the interpreter (keccak and jump analysis). A stale storage word after a hook reentry would change a delta or a pool slot inside unlock.

leads.question: In bor v2.11.1 and develop, can a BlockSTM incarnation read a transient storage word, or a storage word written and then reverted inside a frame, of another transaction through the multi-version store (core/blockstm mvhashmap keys and the parallel StateDB read path)? List the key kinds the store holds and whether transient storage is one of them.
leads.why: L-1254 stayed unanswered and the cycle 3 clearance covers the transient map of one execution. A transient word of an aborted incarnation seen by another transaction would break A1 on the block producer, where eth_call never runs in parallel.

leads.question: Extend the 337 address sweep with the IHooks selector shapes: for each address whose low 14 bits pass isValidHookAddress (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127), eth_call from the PoolManager address with each permitted hook selector and a 64 byte and a 1,000 byte hookData. Does any address return at least 32 bytes that start with the selector, and for the returns-delta flags, a second word that would parse as a delta (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-160)?
